svg.text: SERIES 1 • CARD 08 OF 09 • DOMAIN: UNIT CIRCLE TRIGONOMETRY & PROJECTIONS • DUAL ROTATING CURSOR • (X, Y) PROJECTION WINDOWS
LESSON GUIDE: UNIT CIRCLE TRIGONOMETRY & PROJECTIONS
Grades 9–12 Trigonometry, Pre-Calculus & Physics • Hands-On Classroom & Home STEM Studio Series

text.tspan: Turn the transparent cursor arm to the 30° mark.
Look at the inner radian scale: 30° aligns exactly with π/6 rad.
Notice the right triangle projected onto the unit circle base!
Look down at the horizontal X-axis window:
This is the horizontal base length of the 30°-60°-90° triangle.

g.text: STEPS 3 & 4: READ SINE & VERIFY ON STACKCALC

text.tspan: 3. READ VERTICAL SINE: Look at vertical Y-axis window: Y = sin(30°) = 1/2 = 0.5000.
Calculator Verification: Press Unit Circle Radian Icon ([COS], [SIN] & [↱][▸y,x]) and run 45 [COS] [↰] [x²] 45 [SIN] [↰] [x²] [+] → 1.

g.text: CORE PRINCIPLE: SINE AND COSINE ARE CIRCLE COORDINATES

text.tspan: Textbook right triangles only work for angles < 90°. The volvelle proves that sine and cosine
are the literal (X, Y) coordinates of a point moving around a circle! In Quadrant II, cosine
naturally becomes negative because X is negative, while sine remains positive!
Rotate cursor to 60°. Notice X and Y coordinates swap: X = cos(60°) = 1/2 = 0.500, Y = sin(60°) = √3/2 ≈ 0.866! (Scan QR for 3D animated solution!)

g.text: → Assemble with your physical blocks, then scan the QR code to verify with the 3D step-by-step vector model.
